sentences.text: After seven years and nine planetary flybys, BepiColombo has reached Mercury.
Capture happens not with one big engine burn but through a slow approach lasting weeks: the spacecraft all but glides into Mercury's weak gravity field.
This evening, for the first time, it passes only a few hundred kilometres above the surface; it is now a moon of Mercury.
Over the coming weeks the orbit will tighten a little with every pass; in December Europe's MPO and Japan's Mio will separate and settle into their own science orbits.
The path you are watching is the planned trajectory ESA supplied to JPL Horizons; it is not live telemetry.
